subject: Policy-driven preflight: Terraform / Helm / Ansible review for NimbleHealth private deployment
body:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: NimbleHealth Infra <infra@nimblehealth.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Policy-driven preflight: Terraform / Helm / Ansible review for NimbleHealth private deployment

Hi Aisha / Nimble team —

As we move into the private deployment preflight, attached is a focused checklist that maps our standard policy controls to the modules we plan to ship: Terraform network modules, Helm charts (gateway + telemetry), and Ansible runbooks for node hardening. Key asks for this thread: 

- Can Nimble confirm the egress policy design in networking-diff.tf matches your compliance constraints (no external control-plane callbacks except to our approved registry)?
- We need a quick read on secret handling: are KMS/HSM keys managed by you or should we wire Redwood-managed sealed-secret flow?
- Please flag any policy gaps (audit log retention, SOC2 evidence points) so we can capture in the CI gating job.

Attachments: preflight-checklist.md (policy mappings), networking-diff.tf (proposed tf changes), helm-values-nimble.yaml (chart overrides), ci-gating-pipeline.yml (proposed pipeline gating steps).

Suggested next steps: review the checklist, mark R/G/A on the items you own, and we'll sync for a 30m call if there are >3 red items. If you're fine, we can lift the gating branch into our staging pipeline tomorrow.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

---

On Wed, 17 Feb 2027 at 09:40, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks — quick notes from a runtime/CI perspective after a first pass of the attachments:
>
> - networking-diff.tf: I noticed the transit-gateway module still refers to a shared NAT rule that permits 0.0.0.0/0 egress from the control plane pods. For Nimble's regulated workloads we should restrict to registry IP ranges and AWS health checks only. I added an inline comment at line 78 in the diff.
> - helm-values-nimble.yaml: telemetry sidecar is enabled by default; suggest we make this opt-in until Nimble confirms telemetry export endpoint (PII scrubber in place).
> - ci-gating-pipeline.yml: pipeline should include an automated terratest run in a dry VPC and a policy check job (OPA + conftest) before merging. I can prototype the pipeline step if Nimble approves the dry VPC cost.
>
> Action items I recommend we capture now:
> 1) Narrow egress CIDR for control-plane (owner: nimble infra)
> 2) Confirm KMS integration pattern (owner: nimble infra / redwood security)
> 3) Add conftest OPA rules for module-level secrets (owner: redwood infra)
>
> I can attach a quick terratest example later today.
>
> - Soojin
>
> On Wed, 17 Feb 2027 at 09:02 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com> wrote:
> > (original message)

---

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@nimblehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: NimbleHealth Infra <infra@nimblehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Policy-driven preflight: Terraform / Helm / Ansible review for NimbleHealth private deployment

Thanks Hannah — appreciate the detail.

Quick answers to your asks: 
- Egress: Nimble will restrict control-plane egress to the container registry IP ranges and our monitoring endpoints. I'll send a definitive CIDR list by EOD.
- KMS/HSM: We'll manage the KMS keys in our AWS account (customer-owned). We expect Redwood to integrate via an IAM role and not persist any unencrypted secrets.
- Audit retention: Nimble requires 365 days for control-plane audit logs; happy to review a proposed logging plan.

We have Procurement on the thread but I'll also loop in our compliance lead if there are any SOC2 evidence points that need a contact. Tentatively ok to run your terratest dry VPC assuming we cap runtime to 2 hours.

Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Head of Cloud Ops, NimbleHealth

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aisha.rahman@nimblehealth.com
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 10:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Policy-driven preflight: Terraform / Helm / Ansible review for NimbleHealth private deployment

A couple of pragmatic notes from the module side:

- We should add a module contract that explicitly forbids embedding plaintext ARNs in charts or vars. Add a sentinel policy (or conftest) rule that tests for 'aws_kms_key' references in non-secret outputs.
- For the helm charts: add a values schema (JSON schema) so CI can reject unexpected top-level keys; this prevents accidental enabling of features that open egress.
- Ansible playbooks: split verification tasks from mutate tasks. Verification can be run in read-only mode in the dry VPC.

I'll open two small PRs today: 1) conftest ruleset, 2) helm values schema. If Nimble confirms KMS ownership, I'll wire the IAM role trust doc to the shared drive link.

-Karthik

---

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: aisha.rahman@nimblehealth.com, infra@nimblehealth.com
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 11:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Policy-driven preflight: Terraform / Helm / Ansible review for NimbleHealth private deployment

Thanks all — this is great progress. Summary / decisions from thread: 

- Nimble will provide egress CIDRs by EOD and will manage KMS keys in their account (Redwood to implement IAM role integration).
- Redwood infra to add conftest/OPA rules and a helm values JSON schema; Karthik will raise PRs today.
- Soojin to prepare the terratest dry VPC job and estimate runtime cost for Nimble (cap at 2 hours unless they approve more).
- Marissa to update the CI gating pipeline with a new policy-check stage and reference the conftest rules.

Next steps: Hannah to schedule a 30m sync for Thursday 11am PT if Nimble has >3 red items after they review the checklist. Otherwise we'll proceed to staging pipeline lift on Friday.

I'll attach the IAM trust doc and the conftest rule draft in the follow-up.

Cheers,
Hannah

Attachments referenced in thread: preflight-checklist.md (policy matrix), networking-diff.tf (tf module diff), helm-values-nimble.yaml (overrides), ci-gating-pipeline.yml (pipeline draft)
